Dualize the Fourier coefficients of Rem against a finitely supported unit ell^2 sequence. After absolute values, use F001 and N003 with x_1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f_1(a)| and likewise for slots 2 and 3; take x_4(d) to be the modulus of the dual coefficient at -d. Their norms are bounded by the three H^sigma norms and the unit dual norm. The factor exp(-i*t0*Phi) has modulus one, and the prefactor in Rem is tau/18. Thus ||Rem||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma). A multiplier of modulus <=1 only decreases the absolute majorant, so the same proof covers every stated restriction.

Approximate each mean-zero H^sigma input by its finite Fourier projections. The trilinear bound F002 and the three-term telescoping difference bound show that the outputs are Cauchy in the complete L^2 space, independently of the chosen approximations. This defines a unique bounded trilinear extension and retains the inequality. For smooth inputs it coincides with the original absolutely convergent Fourier expression. At sigma=0 this supplies in particular an L^2-by-L^2-by-L^2 bound C*tau.

For the final clause fix f,w,M0 and temporarily assume L1: 0<sigma<=1,0<tau<=1,w in mean-zero H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M0, f in mean-zero L^2, and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. Apply F003 with exponent sigma to (w,w,w). Expand Rem(f,f,f)-Rem(w,w,w) as Rem(f-w,f,f)+Rem(w,f-w,f)+Rem(w,w,f-w) and apply F003 with exponent zero to each term. The difference is bounded by C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Since ||f||_2<=M0+1, this yields C_(sigma,M0)*tau*(tau^sigma+delta). Discharge L1 and quantify all data. This proves the output assertion.

R005.text: For any mean-zero L^2 f, Cauchy-Schwarz in its Fourier series gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2, and coefficient weights give ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. For a general H^1 function its mean plus this estimate for its derivative gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_(H^1). The product rule then gives ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Apply it to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g and use S_t isometric and P contractive to obtain ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. Each assertion is quantified over inputs in its indicated space.

For L^2 f,g, every Fourier coefficient of the product (S_t f)(S_t g) has modulus <=||f||_2||g||_2 by Cauchy-Schwarz in the convolution. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) proves ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), so ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2. Finally J_t(A0,g) is a product of S_t Dinv A0 in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infinity, followed by contractions, so its L^2 norm is <=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2 by F001. Approximation by polynomials and these continuous bilinear bounds justify the products and their extensions.

For the normal-form clause take smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b]. At k!=0 the coefficient of J_t is sum_(r+s=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*r*s)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiating the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients. Therefore d_t J_t(f,g)=3*B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smooth spatial Fourier series and all derivatives used here converge absolutely, so differentiation and integration are legitimate. Integration gives the displayed two-endpoint normal form. For piecewise smooth continuous paths apply this on each subinterval; intermediate J endpoint values cancel because the paths are continuous.

Symmetry of J is immediate from the product formula. Since Dinv partial_x=P, substitution gives J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}, whose integral on I is exactly Ctri_I(f,g,h); no inverse derivative is commuted through a product. For constant f,g, integrate F003 and multiply by 1/2 to obtain Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_a^t. This establishes every identity asserted in the output assertion.

R006.text: Apply E003 on I=[a,b]. For its first assertion take alpha=0 and any slot i in {1,2,3}. The stated spatially smooth paths, continuous and piecewise smooth in time on a finite compact partition, have bounded L2 norms and bounded piecewise H^(-pstar) derivatives. Integration by parts against a compactly supported smooth scalar time test function on each piece gives their weak derivatives; adjacent endpoint terms cancel by continuity, so there are no jump masses. Thus all three paths satisfy E003's hypotheses. For its second assertion take alpha=sigma, with arbitrary 0<=sigma<=1 and constant H^sigma inputs; their weak derivatives are zero. Put c0=sqrt(2*pi). Every source spatial norm and source X norm is c0 times the corresponding normalized norm. Dividing the source trilinear inequalities by c0 multiplies each constant by c0^2 and preserves time powers, all three negative-norm slots, and uniformity in a,b and the inputs. These are the two asserted normalized Ctri bounds. For completeness, bounded multilinear extensions used here and below follow by approximating inputs in their controlling norms: expand a difference of multilinear outputs as a sum of terms each containing one input difference. The bounds make outputs Cauchy and their limits independent of the approximants, with the same bound. Sobolev Fourier truncations are dense by convergence of the defining weighted square sums, and deleting the zero mode preserves mean zero. This gives the constant-input extensions; for path inputs the same argument gives the extension to the closure of the stated initial domain in its controlling X norm, without assuming density in the entire X space.

H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Define a_gamma by the displayed three-case formula; the three cases give a_gamma in [0,1). First establish the required Sobolev comparison directly from D003: for real q<=r and any u in H^r, each weight (1+k^2)^q is at most (1+k^2)^r. Summing the weighted squared coefficients gives ||u||_(H^q)<=||u||_(H^r), with the identity inclusion on Fourier coefficients. For completions this follows first for Fourier truncations and then by their norm convergence; for the nonnegative exponents used here these inclusions identify the same L2 function. For 0<gamma<1/2 or 1/2<gamma<=1, E005 with sigma=gamma has source a(sigma)=a_gamma and directly gives the product inequality. At gamma=1/2, do not prescribe a numerical source epsilon. E005's 'any sufficiently small positive epsilon' means there is a positive threshold below which all positive choices are permitted; taking half the minimum of such a threshold and 1/8 supplies a permitted epsP with 0<epsP<=1/8. Fix one such epsP independently of f,g. Apply E005 with sigma=1/2 and source a(sigma)=epsP to arbitrary f in H^(1/2) and g in H^(1/8), using the just-proved inclusion H^(1/8) into H^epsP. Its exact conclusion is |f*g|_2<=c_(1/2,epsP)|f|_(1/2)|g|_(epsP), bounded by c_(1/2,epsP)|f|_(1/2)|g|_(1/8). Dividing every bilinear source inequality by c0 changes the constant by c0, and proves F002 with the unchanged a_gamma. The fixed source-dependent epsP is absorbed in C_gamma. No gamma=0 product assertion is needed.

First fix a permitted epsF with 0<epsF<=1/8 for E004's sigma=1/2 case. Such a choice exists because E004 allows every sufficiently small fixed positive epsilon: choose half the minimum of a positive admissibility threshold and 1/8. Fix this choice using E004 alone, independently of all stage data; only the gamma=1/2 case uses it. Fix the arbitrary a,tau,t,w,M0 as declared and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Set wshift=S_a w. The multiplier of S_a has modulus one and is one at frequency zero, so it preserves each H norm and the mean. Its multiplier group law gives B_(a+r)(f,g)=S_(-a)B_r(S_a f,S_a g) for smooth time-independent inputs. Substituting s=a+r in D021 and moving the fixed bounded map S_(-a) through the smooth time integral gives Fstage_(a,t)(w)=S_(-a)Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift), initially for smooth mean-zero w. Apply E004 with sigma=gamma, n=0, timestep tau, s=t-a, f=g=wshift and beta=a_gamma; use epsF at gamma=1/2. Here tau>0 and 0<=t-a<=tau. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and a_gamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0; for gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsF and a_gamma-beta0=5/8+epsF>0; for gamma>1/2 the gap is 1-gamma>=0. In every case a_gamma<=1+gamma. The denominator 1+gamma-beta0 is respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+epsF, and 2, all positive. Thus E004 yields exactly the source powers (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma), (11/8)/(2+epsF), and (1+gamma)/2 in these three cases. Each is at least gamma: in the first case subtracting gamma times the positive denominator from the numerator gives 1/2-gamma/2+gamma^2>0; in the middle case epsF<=1/8 implies (11/8)/(2+epsF)>=11/17>1/2; in the last case 1>=gamma. Since 0<tau<=1, a power at least gamma gives tau to that power at most tau^gamma. Divide the source bilinear estimate by c0, multiplying its constant by c0. Use the isometry S_(-a) and ||wshift||_(H^gamma)=||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 to obtain ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma uniformly over a<=t<=a+tau. These calculations first hold on mean-zero trigonometric polynomials; E004 is bilinear, so the difference and completion argument in S001 extends its bounds and the covariance identity to mean-zero H^gamma inputs. To pass the covariance identity, apply it to Fourier truncations and use the bounded S maps on the source and target Sobolev spaces. All constants are independent of a,t,tau and Fourier support. Taking the supremum in t proves F003; the fixed epsF is absorbed in C_gamma.

Apply E004 to the same wshift and time parameters with beta=1+gamma, retaining the permitted epsF at gamma=1/2. This is the upper endpoint of [beta0,1+gamma]. The positive denominator was checked in S003 and the numerator 1+gamma-beta is zero, so the source power is zero. After division by c0 the exact estimate is ||Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma||wshift||_(H^gamma)^2. The smooth covariance identity established in S003 and the S isometry give the same bound for Fstage_(a,t)(w); the bilinear difference and Fourier completion argument of S001 extends both this bound and the identity to H^gamma inputs, now with target H^(1+gamma). Under L1 the right side is at most C_gamma*M0^2, uniformly in a,t,tau and Fourier support. Enlarge C_(gamma,M0) to cover this bound and F003 (for example a fixed C_gamma*(1+M0^2)). Discharge L1 into the norm-bound antecedent and universally quantify M0,w,tau,a,t. The two target Sobolev extensions agree as distributions because they arise from the same polynomial truncations and H^(1+gamma) includes continuously in H^(a_gamma) by the Fourier norm comparison proved in S002. With F001 and F002 this proves every clause of the output assertion, including the stated extensions. Neither chosen source epsilon occurs in the public input/output.

R007.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

For the endpoint identity now take smooth real mean-zero f and integer n>=0. Apply E006 with precisely this f,n,tau. Its exponential convention agrees with S_(-t), and its F^n and A^n are respectively Fstage and the displayed B integral; its R_2^n is D015 with t0=n*tau. This gives exactly the asserted twisted update. There is no norm conversion in this algebraic identity.

At t=t_n, all stage integrals in Interp vanish and its affine correction is zero, so Vst(t_n)=f. At t=t_n+tau, Q(t) cancels its contribution to W and Vst=f+Fstage+Cst-Rem. With f=v^n, F002 identifies this as v^(n+1). F001 ensures the next state remains smooth and real mean-zero. Thus adjacent pieces have matching endpoints, and the concatenation is continuous and piecewise smooth, real and mean-zero. This proves the output assertion.

R008.text: Fix the local a,tau,M0,f,w, and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1, hence q=tau^gamma+delta<=2 and ||f||_2<=M0+1. Take the tuple from Interp and the exponent a_gamma from N006. By the endpoint formula in N005, F(t)=(1/6)[J_s(f,f)]_a^t. The J:H^0 times H^0->H^1 bound gives sup||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0). Expanding J(f,f)-J(w,w) as J(f-w,f)+J(w,f-w) gives sup||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Since a_gamma<1, N006 now yields sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Also z=f+F has bounded L^2 norm and z'=F'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), whose H^(-pstar) norm is bounded by N005, so ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

Set Astage=Fstage_(a,t)(w) and Dstage=F-Astage. Apply the product bound in N006 to partial_x(S_t Astage) and S_t Astage, using the H^(1+gamma) and H^(a_gamma) stage bounds. It gives ||partial_x[(S_t Astage)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||Astage||_(H^(1+gamma))||Astage||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma. The difference of squares is (S_t Dstage)*S_t(F+Astage). The H^1 algebra estimate in N005 and F001 give its derivative norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Therefore sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Integrating yields sup||Q||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. N004 with exponent gamma and the current f,w then bounds Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f) by the same quantity, so ||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

Since Dinv B_t(f,F)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F)], split f=w+(f-w). N006 bounds the w product by C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q using F001. For the other product use ||f-w||_2||S_t F||_infinity<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta by the uniform H^1 stage bound and N005. Thus sup||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Differentiating the definition Y=Cst+Q-((t-a)/tau)W gives Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau. N005, F002 and this asymmetric product estimate give sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. As Y(a)=0, integration gives sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

Apply the normal form of N005 to Cst=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds, with f constant, F(a)=0 and F'=(1/2)B(f,f). Symmetry and the J(B,h)-to-Ctri identity give exactly Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f). Its J term is O(q) in L^2 by N005 and F001. In its Ctri term use N006 with exponent gamma on (w,w,w) to get O(tau^gamma). Expand the difference from (f,f,f) into three trilinear differences and use N006 with exponent zero on each; their size is O(delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2). Thus sup||Cst||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. With F002 in Y=Cst+Q-affine W this gives sup||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

All stage components are mean-zero because B and Rem have zero output mean. N005 gives ||Y'||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y'||_2 and ||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y||_2. Combine F003 and F004 to obtain ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. These constants depend only on gamma and M0; none uses a higher norm of f.
Collect F001-F005. Discharge L1 and universally quantify all the step data. This proves every clause of the output assertion.

R009.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. First fix a step with the antecedent L1 of N008: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with smooth real mean-zero f,w, M0>=1 and the stated a,tau. Use its tuple and q. Differentiation of Interp gives Vst'=(1/2)B_t(z,z)-W/tau. Since Vst=z+Y, subtraction of (1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst) gives rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau. The residual increment vanishes at a. N008 bounds ||Y||_2 by C*q, ||z||_2 by C and ||W||_2/tau by C*q, with q<=2. N005 thus gives ||rho'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

For the first integral in rho apply N005's normal form to (Y,z). Its boundary J terms are O(tau*q) using ||Dinv Y||_2<=C*tau*q from N008 and bounded ||z||_2. The integral containing Y' is O(tau*q) by the asymmetric J bound and ||Dinv Y'||_2<=C*q. Since z'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), symmetry turns the remaining term into a fixed multiple of Ctri_[a,t](f,f,Y). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y: N008 gives ||Y||_X<=C*q and ||Y||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q, while f is constant with L^2 norm <=M0+1. Hence this term too is O(tau*q), even on a partial step.

For integral B(Y,Y), apply the same normal form with Y in both slots. Boundary terms use ||Dinv Y||_2||Y||_2<=C*tau*q^2, and derivative integrals use ||Dinv Y'||_2||Y||_2<=C*q^2 over length tau. Thus it is O(tau*q^2)=O(tau*q) because q<=2. The affine W term is O(tau*q) by N008. Combine with F001-F002 to prove both residual estimates on the whole or any initial part of the step. Discharge L1 and quantify the data.

Now fix a smooth numerical trajectory and exact twisted v and assume L2: sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h<=1 and E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. N007 gives the continuous interpolation V with grid values v^n. Concatenate the residual increments, obtaining Rres and V'=(1/2)B(V,V)+Rres' stepwise and distributionally. At each intersected step start t_n, delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I, so its q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I and F003 applies with w=v(t_n),f=v^n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps; the last can be partial. Sum the step increment bounds to obtain sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also sup||Rres'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

Under L2, ||v||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0 and ||V||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0+1. Subtract the equations to obtain e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 and F004 imply ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), so ||e||_X has the same bound. The exact equation bounds ||v'||_(H^(-pstar)), and V=v-e then has bounded X norm too, since tau^gamma+E_I<=2. This proves the remaining assertions. Discharge L2 and quantify the trajectory and interval.

R010.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj equal to the identity operator minus Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), using F001: their total contribution is <=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

For the remaining integral in F003 substitute the actual stepwise Rres' formula from N009, and use integral J(B,h)=Ctri from N005 on each intersected step segment. It becomes -Ctri(Y_n,z_n,V)-(1/2)Ctri(Y_n,Y_n,V)-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds. At that step's start, delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C*q_n, ||Y_n||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C and ||W_n||_2<=C*tau*q_n. N006, with the negative norm on Y_n, bounds the first two terms by C*tau*q_n (using q_n<=2 and ||V||_X<=C from F001). The last term is also <=C*tau*q_n by the L^2 J bound from N005. These remain valid upper bounds on a partial final step. At most h/tau+1 steps are met, and q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I. Thus the forcing integral is bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

Combine F003-F005 to obtain sup||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. With F002, the exact error identity and residual bound in F001 give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All constants are uniform in the parameters specified in F005.

Choose C0>=1 dominating these constants from F005-F006, independently of all the particular paths. Define N0=ceil(max(2,16*C0,(16*C0)^(1/pstar))). Then C0*(N0^(-1)+N0^(-pstar))<=1/8<=1/4. Put delta0=min(1,1/(8*C0*(N0^2+3))) and K0=4*C0. If h<=delta0 and tau<=delta0/2, then C0*(N0^2*h+h+tau)<=C0*delta0*(N0^2+3)<=1/8<=1/4. F006 therefore has E_I coefficient at most 1/2.
